subject: Television & Streaming
title: AMC's Golden Age on a Budget
description: A short lesson to help you apply AMC's Golden Age on a Budget.

hook.text: AMC was a channel that showed old movies nobody watched.

buildup.text: Mad Men won 16 Emmys and made AMC culturally relevant.

discovery.text: AMC proved that a small cable channel could compete with HBO-level quality.

twist.text: Despite critical acclaim, AMC struggled financially.

climax.text: AMC's story shows television's paradox: the shows that define an era aren't always the ones that pay the bills.

punchline.text: A movie channel made the best TV and almost went broke doing it.

quiz.question: What paradox did AMC's experience with prestige television reveal?
options: Critically acclaimed shows define an era but don't always generate enough revenue
Cable channels can't produce quality content
